lesson_title: The Secret Life of a Cooldrink Bottle
hook_text: You drink it in two minutes. The bottle could still be around in three hundred years.
clip_script: A plastic cooldrink bottle starts as oil or gas deep underground. It is light, tough and waterproof, perfect for a drink. Two minutes later it is empty. Now what? The tiny living things that rot away food cannot eat plastic. So a bottle tossed away lasts for hundreds of years. Sun and waves crack it into microplastics, smaller than a grain of rice, now found in fish, in seabirds and even in drinking water. Turtles eat plastic bags because they look like jellyfish. After big storms, Durban's beaches have been buried in plastic washed down rivers. The fix starts with you. Reduce: skip the straw. Reuse: carry your own bottle. Recycle: look for the number 1 on the bottom. And when you see a waste picker, remember they collect most of South Africa's recycling.
visual_style: Whiteboard timeline from an oil well to a bottle to a beach, with a clock spinning to 300 years; the bottle shattering into tiny dots that drift into a fish; a turtle mistaking a bag for a jellyfish; a recycling triangle with a 1.
pacing: Fast production, a long slow decay, an upbeat action ending.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and follow the life story of everything you throw away.
